worst_places.quote: Pages Router is legacy and should not be used in new projects; App Router is the recommended approach
worst_places.problem: nextjs-quiz-3 asks "When should you use the Pages Router over the App Router in a new Next.js project?" and the only correct answer refuses the question — a scenario item with no scenario in any option. It also contradicts the zone's own article: content/topics/nextjs/en/03-app-router-vs-page-router.md says "the Pages Router is officially supported and used in a huge number of existing codebases — so knowing both isn't 'history', it's a practical skill", and "you're more likely to encounter the Pages Router in a real project than to start fresh with the App Router". «Legacy» is the article's word for the codebases, not for the router.
worst_places.before: Pages Router is legacy and should not be used in new projects; App Router is the recommended approach
worst_places.after: For a genuinely new project, App Router — it is the recommended default since 13.4. Pages Router is still officially supported, so you pick it only to match an existing codebase

worst_places.quote: Next.js App Router defaults to caching fetch requests indefinitely via the Data Cache layer. These cached requests persist across deployments and rebuilds until explicitly revalidated using revalidateTag() or revalidatePath(). Option 1 is correct.
worst_places.problem: nextjs-quiz-18, and nextjs-quiz-8 makes the same claim. content/topics/nextjs/en/05-data-fetching-caching-revalidation.md has a section headed "A major change in Next.js 15" stating that fetch() defaults to force-cache in 13/14 and to no-store in 15, and content/questions/nextjs.json hedges persistence to "in some setups, deployments, if persistent storage is configured". The quiz states the v14 behaviour as timeless fact and hardens the hedge into "persist across deployments and rebuilds". Also "Option 1 is correct" is a position reference that shuffleOptions invalidates on the random-quiz route.
worst_places.before: Next.js App Router defaults to caching fetch requests indefinitely via the Data Cache layer. These cached requests persist across deployments and rebuilds until explicitly revalidated using revalidateTag() or revalidatePath(). Option 1 is correct.
worst_places.after: In Next.js 13 and 14 a fetch() with no cache option defaults to force-cache: the result goes into the Data Cache and is reused until you revalidate it with revalidateTag() or revalidatePath(). (Next.js 15 flipped this default to no-store — one of its most discussed breaking changes.) Whether the Data Cache survives a deploy depends on your hosting: it needs persistent storage.

worst_places.quote: ISR allows static pages to be regenerated on-demand when they're requested, using the revalidate option in getStaticProps.
worst_places.problem: nextjs-quiz-27 explains ISR through getStaticProps. nextjs-quiz-11's explanation, eight items earlier, says "The `getStaticProps` API doesn't exist in App Router—it's Pages Router only", and nextjs-quiz-22 keys getServerSideProps wrong for being "Pages Router syntax". Every other item in the bank is framed in App Router terms. The reader is taught to reject Pages Router data APIs in three items and then handed one as the explanation of ISR.
worst_places.before: ISR allows static pages to be regenerated on-demand when they're requested, using the revalidate option in getStaticProps.
worst_places.after: ISR lets a static page be regenerated on demand when it is next requested. In the App Router you set `export const revalidate = 60` on the route segment, or pass `next: { revalidate: 60 }` to fetch; the Pages Router equivalent was the revalidate field returned from getStaticProps.

worst_places.problem: nextjs-quiz-8's stem has no ``` fence — the language tag `tsx` sits on its own line as prose, so the whole snippet renders as an unformatted paragraph on a phone. nextjs-quiz-21 and nextjs-quiz-26 have the same defect in both locales. Separately, the code itself is wrong: `data` is the Response object, never `.json()`-ed, and is rendered directly into JSX — three items in a row ship code that would not run.

worst_places.quote: The fetch request executes on the server, eliminating the need to expose API endpoints to the client and reducing bundle size
worst_places.problem: nextjs-quiz-17's keyed answer says the advantage is not exposing an API endpoint — but the stem's code is `await fetch('/api/users/${userId}')`, i.e. it calls an API endpoint, and a relative URL in a Server Component throws in Next.js because there is no base URL on the server. The stem demonstrates the opposite of the lesson and does not run. A middle developer who has hit this exact error will read the item as wrong and stop trusting the bank.
worst_places.before:
const user = await fetch(`/api/users/${userId}`);
  const data = await user.json();
worst_places.after: const data = await db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });

patterns: The strongest position bias of the three banks and possibly of the site. correctIndex is 0 in 29 of 30 items — the single exception is nextjs-quiz-26 — and the correct option is strictly the longest in 24 of 30. On the per-topic route, where shuffleOptions is not applied, a reader who always picks the first, longest answer scores 29/30 without reading a single question. The shape is visible in the data too: correct options carry two or three coordinated clauses ("automatically resizes and serves optimized formats (WebP) based on device, preventing layout shift with aspect ratio control") while distractors are single claims.

Half the bank asks four questions. Six items are "why use next/image instead of " (4, 9, 14, 19, 25, 29) with near-identical correct options; three are "what is middleware for" (10, 23, 30); five are ISR/fetch caching (2, 8, 18, 24, 27); three are Server vs Client Component (1, 6, 15). The repetition is where the contradictions live — items 6 and 17 give opposite verdicts on bundle-size reduction, items 11 and 27 give opposite verdicts on getStaticProps, and five caching items state a v14 default that the zone's own article documents as changed in v15. Meanwhile Server Actions, streaming/Suspense, parallel and intercepting routes, error boundaries, metadata and generateMetadata get zero items.

Russian is machine output that was never opened. Eight items carry tokens that exist in no language: «переvalidation», «переvalidates», «переvalidate» (six items, including one in a question stem and two in keyed-correct options), «переваиливаются», «теку». The English side of the same items is clean, so this is a translation pass that shipped without a proof-read — and it lands hardest on `revalidate`, the single most important word in a Next.js caching quiz.
notes: Scores are per locale for the whole bank. E is scored 2 rather than 3 because three of thirty stems (8, 21, 26) render their code as prose for want of a ``` fence, and 17's snippet throws at runtime. G is scored 1 because the artifacts are in keyed-correct options and question stems, not just prose, so they block answering, not merely reading. No item lacks a correct option and no model self-talk was found. Item ids are contiguous 1-30, unlike the react and nodejs banks. nextjs-quiz-28's explanation ends "This combines static generation with type safety" — type safety is unrelated to generateStaticParams and to everything else in the item.
